Effective number of independent traits

Source: R/gwas.R
indri_effective_tests.Rd

Galwey's (2009) effective number of tests, from the eigenvalues lambda of the Spearman correlation matrix of the traits: (sum(sqrt(lambda)))^2 / sum(lambda). It is 1 for perfectly correlated traits and ncol(Y) for independent ones, and is the factor adjust = "effective" multiplies single-trait p-values by in indri_gwas().

Usage

indri_effective_tests(Y, X = NULL)

Arguments

Y

Numeric matrix, individuals by traits.

X

Optional fixed-effects design, as in indri_gwas().

Value

A number between 1 and ncol(Y).

Details

With a design X, the correlation is that of the residuals of Y on X: the single-trait tests see the traits after the fixed effects, and covariates shared by the traits (sex, age, line) would otherwise make them look more correlated than they are to the tests.

References

Galwey, N. W. (2009). A new measure of the effective number of tests, a practical tool for comparing families of non-independent significance tests. Genetic Epidemiology 33, 559-568. doi:10.1002/gepi.20408
